subject: Day 9: weight curve up; latch troubleshooting if needed
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 9. Weight is climbing if feeds are effective; most term infants are back to birth weight by day 14. If today's diaper count is below six wet or below three stools (breastfeeding) by mid-afternoon, escalate. The mother's bleeding should be lochia serosa now — lighter pink-brown, less than menstrual flow.

Action items
- If latch pain has not resolved, schedule an in-person IBCLC consult this week. Bring the feeding log. International Lactation Consultant Association directory: https://ilca.org/
- If formula-feeding, target 2-3 oz every 3-4 hours by today. CDC on infant formula preparation and storage: https://www.cdc.gov/infant-toddler-nutrition/formula-feeding/index.html
- Confirm Avi's name and Social Security number are on your tax records for the year. The SSN may have arrived by mail this week if SS-5 was filed at the hospital.
- Continue the feeding log.
- If both parents are home, formalize a sleep-shift schedule. Day 9 onward is when stress and sleep debt compound. ACOG postpartum care overview: https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/postpartum-pain-management

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Cord stump still attached and drying. Cluster feeding 60-90 minutes in the evening. Baby acne peaking. Single black meconium stool stuck in a diaper days after the transition.
- [low concern] Mother's bleeding now pink-brown or rust-colored, lighter than menstrual flow.
- [monitor] Cord stump leaking yellow or surrounding skin red. Mother's bleeding suddenly heavier or saturated pads.
- [call within 24h] Yellow tinge still spreading or visible on legs. Fewer than six wet diapers in a day. Persistent latch pain with cracks or frank blood. Weight not climbing despite adequate feeds (call pediatrician for a weight check). AAP HealthyChildren on jaundice: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Jaundice.aspx
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusal of all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunity
Narrate one ordinary task in detail during Avi's next awake-alert window. Conversational turns (not raw word count) predict later language outcomes. Romeo et al. 2018 in Psych Science: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/

Upcoming
- Day 5-15: cord stump dries and detaches.
- Day 14: most infants are back to birth weight by today.
- Day 14-21: first common growth spurt.
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit window opens.

Further reading
- International Lactation Consultant Association directory: https://ilca.org/
- CDC on infant formula preparation: https://www.cdc.gov/infant-toddler-nutrition/formula-feeding/index.html
- AAP HealthyChildren on jaundice: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Jaundice.aspx
- The Happiest Baby on the Block by Harvey Karp: https://www.happiestbaby.com/pages/dr-harvey-karp

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Quiets or turns toward a familiar voice
  AAP window: day 7-45
  What to look for: Voice recognition begins before birth; postnatally it shows as orienting or settling to a parent's voice.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/recognizes-parent-voice/complete

- Watches your face when you talk
  AAP window: day 7-60
  What to look for: Baseline social orientation. Look for sustained gaze, even briefly, during alert windows.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-face-briefly/complete

- Moves both arms and both legs
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Symmetric, spontaneous movement of all four limbs. Asymmetry warrants pediatric attention.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-arms-and-legs/complete

- Reacts to loud sounds (startle, blink, stillness)
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Confirms intact hearing response. Universal newborn hearing screen catches most cases but daily observation matters.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/responds-to-loud-sound/complete

- Brings hands within range of eyes and mouth
  AAP window: day 0-45
  What to look for: Early body awareness. Not yet purposeful — looks like accidental discovery.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/brings-hands-near-face/complete
